:::{#def-contour-line}
#### Contour line

For a function $g$ of two real variables $b$ and $c$
and a number $k$,
the **contour line**
[@wikipedia_contour_line]
of $g$ at height $k$
is the set of points where $g$ equals $k$:

$$\cb{(b, c) : g(b, c) = k}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-contour-line}
#### Contour lines of a bowl

For $g(b, c) = b^2 + c^2$,
the contour line at height $k = 4$ is $\cb{(b, c) : b^2 + c^2 = 4}$,
the circle of radius $2$ around $(0, 0)$:
for example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
g(2, 0) &= 4 + 0 \\
&= 4
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
g(0, -2) &= 0 + 4 \\
&= 4.
\end{aligned}
$$

The contour line at height $k = -1$ is empty,
because $b^2 + c^2 \ge 0$ for all $b$ and $c$.

```{r}
#| label: contour-line-alt
#| echo: false
# The alt text, saved once for the figure and its interactive widget.
fig_alt_contour_bowl <- paste(
  "Contour plot of g(b, c) = b squared plus c squared,",
  "with the first coordinate b on the horizontal axis",
  "and the second coordinate c on the vertical axis.",
  "The contour lines at heights 1, 4 and 9 are concentric circles",
  "of radius 1, 2 and 3 around the origin.",
  "Two dots mark the points (2, 0) and (0, -2) on the circle at height 4."
)
```

:::{#fig-contour-line}

```{r}
#| label: contour-line-plot
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt_contour_bowl
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 5
library(ggplot2)

# The bowl g(b, c) = b^2 + c^2 on a grid, and the two points of the example.
bowl <- expand.grid(
  b = seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 200),
  c = seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 200)
)
bowl$g <- bowl$b^2 + bowl$c^2
on_circle <- data.frame(b = c(2, 0), c = c(0, -2))

contour_plot <- ggplot(bowl) +
  aes(b, c) +
  geom_contour(
    aes(z = g, colour = factor(after_stat(level))),
    breaks = c(1, 4, 9)
  ) +
  geom_point(data = on_circle, size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "height k", end = 0.85) +
  coord_fixed(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "first coordinate, b", y = "second coordinate, c") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  htmltools::div(
    role = "img",
    `aria-label` = fig_alt_contour_bowl,
    plotly::ggplotly(contour_plot) |>
      plotly::layout(
        legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0.5, xanchor = "center", y = -0.25)
      ) |>
      plotly::config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
  )
} else {
  contour_plot
}
```

The contour lines of $g(b, c) = b^2 + c^2$ at heights $1$, $4$ and $9$.
The dots mark the two points of the example on the circle at height $4$.
:::
